product: commentary — no product. Reveals why before/after photos are the best native ad image.
hook: The before/after image itself — "a real change, not a product."
body: People stop scrolling because they see a real change, not a product; change creates curiosity, product shots cause scrolling. The long primary text then tells the full story — what was tried, what failed, what finally worked — with the product entering near the end, after the story has done the emotional work. The click goes to an advertorial on the same angle. Leading with product makes you just another ad; leading with transformation and story gets read to the end before the reader realizes they're being sold to.
idea: Lead with the transformation, not the product — curiosity about the change carries the reader past their ad-defenses.
sequencing: Before/after image stops the scroll via curiosity about the change.
Long primary text opens the struggle story.
Product enters near the end as what finally worked.
Advertorial on the same angle carries the story to the close.
formatting: Before/after static + long primary text → advertorial; two photos attached.
why_it_works: Curiosity gap (what caused the change?) plus narrative transportation — readers finish the story before their skepticism engages.
what_to_steal: Before/after for LC: green-stained skin / faded fast-fashion necklace vs. LC piece after months of daily wear, product revealed late in the copy.

product: commentary — no product. Promotes MakeUGC's AI before/after generator workflow (reply-bait).
hook: "Before/after content used to take months to shoot. Now it's one prompt."
body: AI generates before and after states of the same person from one uploaded photo — no real transformation, no waiting, no client shoot. Pitched as the exact format that stops the scroll for fitness, supplement, and wellness brands. Workflow: upload one photo, generate the before/after states, add product, script, and CTA — done in minutes. Reply-bait CTA for the workflow.
idea: AI collapses before/after production from months to minutes.
sequencing: Old way: months to shoot a transformation.
New way: one prompt, same person, two AI states.
why_it_works: Before/after is the highest-proof format; removing production friction multiplies output volume.
what_to_steal: AI before/after for LC: same model wearing a faded fast-fashion piece vs. the LC piece after months — or green-stain skin vs. clean skin.

product: An unnamed hair care client's product (anti-brass treatment for hard-water blonde hair) — the post is a UGC creator's portfolio breakdown of the ad.
hook: not in file (portfolio breakdown post, not the ad script itself).
body: A before/after mixed with testimonial format that performed well for a hair care client. Three components per concept: the payoff, how the product makes her feel more confident, and how it fits into her routine. Targeting is hyper-specific: women in their late 20s with blonde hair and hard water who want to remove brassy tones — showing the transformation and the routine.
idea: Before/after plus testimonial plus routine-fit, aimed at one hyper-specific persona.
sequencing: Show how it makes her feel (confidence).
Show how it fits her routine.
Aim all three at one narrow persona.
why_it_works: Specificity ("hard water blondes") makes the viewer feel the ad was made for her; transformation plus emotion plus routine covers proof, feeling, and feasibility.
what_to_steal: The 3-component structure for LC before/after: payoff shot (stack on wrist), confidence line, routine fit (shower / gym / ocean-proof).

product: commentary — no product (post promotes a top-50 before/after swipe file); the attached example video is a turmeric joint-pain supplement ad for arthritis/knee pain (brand unnamed in transcript).
hook: Post: "BEFORE → AFTER ADS ARE PRINTING 👀" / video: "I asked my husband to help me off the toilet… he packed a bag that night and drove away. I was 52 and I couldn't stand up on my own."
body: The post offers a top-50 before/after swipe file via reply bait. The attached example video is a long-form before/after story ad: a 52-year-old woman who couldn't stand on her own, abandoned by her husband, whose nurse sister reveals her turmeric was useless — she needed 95% curcumin with black pepper for absorption (hers was 2%).
cta: "Reply \"BEFORE\" and I'll send the swipe file."
idea: Before/after works hardest as a long emotional story with a mechanism reveal, not just two photos.
sequencing: Video opens on rock-bottom stakes (can't stand, husband leaves).
Expert reveal: wrong turmeric — needs 95% curcumin plus black pepper.
formatting: Photos plus 21s and 221s vertical videos (720x1280); long-form story video.
why_it_works: Stakes plus a mechanism reveal (why the old solution failed) make the transformation feel earned and credible.
what_to_steal: The mechanism-reveal beat for LC: "your old jewelry failed because of X (thin plating); LC works because of Y (PVD over steel)" inside a before/after story.

product: commentary — no product. A "marketing engineering" pipeline for mass-producing before/after statics (SaaS example).
hook: "Marketing Engineering you can do today — before and after static ads for your saas."
body: Pipeline: scrape Reddit threads via the Exa AI API for pain points and desired outcomes; build a branded before/after template (brand fonts/colors); generate statics with an image model; store every ad's JSON plus variables in Postgres for a recursive loop; bulk-upload to Facebook via API into one ad set; prune losers, let winners keep spending; let winners influence the next round (truncated).
idea: Before/after statics as an automated, data-driven production loop — scrape, generate, upload, prune, recurse.
sequencing: Scrape Reddit for pains and desired outcomes.
Store ad JSON plus variables in Postgres.
Bulk-upload via API into one ad set.
formatting: Before/after static template in brand style; photo attached.
why_it_works: Real voice-of-customer pains plus infinite cheap variations plus ruthless pruning equals creative Darwinism.
what_to_steal: The loop for LC: scrape Reddit and reviews for tarnish complaints → before/after template → generate → prune → recurse.
